justifications.decision: The a is construed as the negative prefix attached to the absolutive hatvā from √han, not as a separate vocative particle. This is required by the contrast with the second half’s positive hatvā, “having killed.” Commentary is unavailable, so the decision rests on grammar and the MW entries for a and √han.
options_considered: negative absolutive a-hatvā, “not having killed / without killing”
separate vocative particle a plus hatvā, “O..., having killed”

justifications.decision: The compound is taken as a bahuvrīhi: mahān anubhāvo yeṣām, “those whose dignity/authority is great.” MW gives mahat as “great” and anubhāva as “dignity, authority, consequence.” Commentary is unavailable.
justifications.chosen: mahānubhāvān qualifies gurūn as “of great dignity/nobility”

justifications.decision: śreyaḥ is construed as neuter nominative singular with an implied asti and the infinitive bhoktum: “it is better to eat.” It is not the object of bhoktum; bhaikṣyam fills that object role. Commentary is unavailable; MW s.v. śreyas supports “better, preferable.”
options_considered: predicate adjective: “it is better/preferable to eat...”
direct object: “to eat the better thing...”

justifications.decision: api most naturally scopes over the immediately preceding object bhaikṣyam, so the half-verse says that even alms are preferable to killing the teachers. Commentary is unavailable; the decision rests on word order and syntax.
options_considered: api with the whole clause: “also, here in the world...”

justifications.decision: The compound is taken adjectivally with kāma in its common final-member sense “desirous of”: arthaḥ kāmo yeṣām. It qualifies gurūn. It is not taken as a separate object “wealth and pleasures,” since its accusative masculine plural agreement and position fit gurūn. Commentary is unavailable; MW s.v. artha gives “advantage/use/aim,” and MW s.v. kāma gives “wish, desire” and supports desire-construals. The verifier’s report did not derive an alternative form, but only gave a tool_error/unsupported-compound notice, so this grammatical decision is retained.
options_considered: dvandva-like “wealth and pleasures” as an object of killing or enjoying

justifications.decision: eva strengthens iha, so the second half contrasts immediate worldly enjoyment with the prior alternative of alms in this world. Commentary is unavailable; MW s.v. eva supports emphatic “just, very, only,” and MW s.v. iha gives “here; in this world.”
options_considered: eva strengthening iha: “right here, in this very world/life”
eva limiting the object bhogān: “only the enjoyments”
justifications.chosen: ihaiva = “right here / in this very world or life”

justifications.decision: The finite verb is VidhiLiṅ, first singular, with Arjuna as subject and bhogān as object. The optative is translated “I would enjoy,” expressing the unacceptable consequence of killing the teachers. Commentary is unavailable; the decision rests on verbal morphology.

The compound is an instrumental tatpuruṣa: rudhireṇa pradigdhāḥ, “smeared with blood,” qualifying bhogān. It is not merely “blood-red.” Commentary is unavailable; MW s.v. rudhira includes “blood/bloody,” and MW s.v. pra-√dih gives “to smear over, besmear.” The verifier’s report did not derive an alternative form, but only gave a tool_error/unsupported-compound notice, so this grammatical decision is retained.

translation:
For, without killing the teachers, men of great dignity,
it is better to eat even alms here in this world.
But, having killed the teachers who desire gain,
I would enjoy, right here, pleasures smeared with blood.
one_shot_delta: No Śaṅkara-bhāṣya line is supplied for this unit, so there is no commentary-specific semantic correction to import.
A mechanically segmented translation could split a + hatvā and produce “having killed” in the first half, missing the essential contrast: ahatvā means “without killing.”
A commentary-blind or morphology-light rendering could take artha-kāmān as “wealth and pleasures” rather than as an adjective of gurūn, “desiring gain/wealth.”
It could also miss that śreyaḥ is the predicate “better,” with bhaikṣyam as the object of bhoktum: “it is better to eat even alms.”
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 segmented gurūn_a_hatvā; I take ahatvā as one negative absolutive, a- + hatvā, because the syntax requires “without killing the teachers,” not a separate vocative particle a plus “having killed.”
ByT5 split mahā_anubhāvān; I analyze the printed mahānubhāvān as one compound stem mahānubhāva, accusative masculine plural, qualifying gurūn.
ByT5 split artha_kāmān; I analyze artha-kāmān as one compound adjective qualifying gurūn, “desiring gain/wealth.”
ByT5 split rudhira_pradigdhān; I analyze rudhira-pradigdhān as one compound adjective qualifying bhogān, “smeared with blood.”
ByT5 tagged bhuñjīya as SPr1O; I normalize the form as VidhiLin, Kartari, Uttama Eka: “I would/should enjoy.”
open_questions: The commentary is explicitly silent for this unit; nuances such as whether artha means specifically “wealth” or more broadly “gain/advantage” cannot be fixed from commentary evidence here.

The Pāṇinian verifier reported tool_error/unsupported-compound notices for artha-kāmān and rudhira-pradigdhān, but supplied no successful contrary derivation; therefore the compound stems, cases, numbers, and relations are retained with notes.
